authors: Joseph L. Mahoney, Håkan Stattin, Heather Lord
title: Unstructured youth recreation centre participation and antisocial behaviour development: Selection influences and the moderating role of antisocial peers
key_finding: center participation → significant INCREASE in antisocial behaviour over 2 y for boys AND girls after selection controls (Örebro, N=1,163); centres aggregating many antisocial peers worst
board3_verdict: THE POOL-BLOCK WARNING: unstructureddrop-in youth centres can RAISE antisocial behavior — peer-aggregation beats supervision when programming is unstructured

authors: Garen J. Wintemute, Mona A. Wright
title: Swimming Pool Owners' Opinions of Strategies for Prevention of Drowning
key_finding: 86% of 795 Sacramento pool-owner households favor CPR training; 85% favor barrier ordinances (80% response)
board3_verdict: the municipal pool-safety lane: barrier ordinances + CPR carry owner support, not resistance

title: Swimming pool immersion accidents: an analysis from the Brisbane Drowning Study
key_finding: 74% of 66 pool immersion accidents in in-ground backyard pools; in-ground accident rate ~5x above-ground when unfenced
board3_verdict: fencing (the barrier law) is the aquatic-band lever — the safety lane, not the crime lane

title: Impact of skin cancer prevention on outdoor aquatics staff: the Pool Cool program in Hawaii and Massachusetts
key_finding: RCT among aquatic staff at 28 outdoor pool sites (HI, MA): sun-protection education improved staff sun-safety behaviors
board3_verdict: the only municipal-pool-site cluster trial recovered: pool sites are feasible trial venues (behavior lane, not crime lane)

title: Knowing how to swim and drowning prevention in children aged 10 to 14 years. Systematic review
key_finding: 'knowing how to swim' measured inconsistently across studies; association with lower drowning risk real but hetero-operator
board3_verdict: learn-to-swim: direction affirmed, magnitude unpoolable — the aquatic-band honest-null

title: Skill Acquisition in the Swimming Pool
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus
board3_verdict: adjacent lane (motor learning)

title: Skate Parks as a Context for Adolescent Development
key_finding: skate-park users reported levels of personal adjustment and social integration SIMILAR to other adolescents (3 studies: interview, observation, questionnaire)
board3_verdict: THE SKATEPARK-FOUNDATION CLAUSE: the flagship triad finds NO deviance deficit in users — null on psychosocial harm, positive on integration

title: Skate-Park Builds, Teenaphobia and the Adolescent Need for Hang-Out Spaces: The Social Utility and Functionality of Urban Skate Parks
key_finding: skate-park builds as the social utility of hang-out space for adolescents; qualitative + ethnographic (no effect sizes in corpus abstract)
board3_verdict: design lane: parks answer 'teenaphobia' by giving youth legit territory — the mechanism claim, unquantified

title: Skatepark injuries and the influence of skatepark design: a one year consecutive case series.
key_finding: 102 injury episodes / 100 subjects over 1 y at a commercial park; injury type/distribution patterned by park design and user skill
board3_verdict: the safety edge of the board band: design matters for injury — the outcome literature here is INJURY, not crime

title: Surface Tensions: Skate-Stoppers and the Surveillance Politics of Small Spaces
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus (qualitative design analysis)
board3_verdict: the anti-skate counter-poll: hostile architecture as the cities' negative spend on the same youth

authors: Nessler JA, Lundquist AL, Jimenez NC, Newcomer SC.
title: Heart Rate Response and Locomotor Activity of Female Skateboarders, BIPOC Skateboarders, and Non-skateboard Users During a Typical Session at a Community Skatepark
key_finding: skatepark sessions meet or exceed CDC exercise-recommendation heart rates; extendable to female/BIPOC users
board3_verdict: the physical-activity dividend: the board band pays in MVPA, measured physiologically

authors: Glenney B, Bjorke I, Buchetti A.
title: Skateboarding and the surplus value of city play
venue: Frontiers in sports and active living
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus
board3_verdict: grey-space theory lane

title: Public Library Summer Reading Programs Contribute to Reading Progress and Proficiency
venue: Evidence Based Library and Information Practice
key_finding: 357 4th-graders, 11 US sites, 3-y mixed-methods: library-school summer-reading partnerships → reading progress/proficiency gains (mixed-methods, no single pooled ES in abstract)
board3_verdict: the library-band flagship: the summer-slide countermeasure the Dominican study later qualified — direction positive, size contested by Overstating Summer Reading Impact

title: Overstating Summer Reading Impact: The Dominican Study
key_finding: reanalysis finds the Dominican study overstated summer-reading impact
board3_verdict: the library-band skeptics' clause: the gains are smaller than claimed

title: An Exploratory Study of the Effect of a Public Library Summer Reading Club on Reading Skills
key_finding: 1966 first-generation summer-reading-club experiment: reading-skill gains in participants (exploratory design)
board3_verdict: the 60-year-old ancestor of the lane: the question has been open and direction-positive since 1966

title: Summer Reading and the Potential Contribution of the Public Library in Improving Reading for Children of Poverty
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus
board3_verdict: UK framing paper for the reading-loss lane

title: Colleges and Community Crime: An Analysis of Campus Proximity and Neighborhood Crime Rates
key_finding: campus PROXIMITY → higher neighborhood violent AND property crime (multilevel negative binomial, National Neighborhood Crime Survey)
board3_verdict: THE FACILITY-PROXIMITY CLAUSE: gathering infrastructure raises nearby crime via opportunity (routine-activity) — the closest peer-reviewed analog to the pool/library proximity question, and it points the OTHER way

title: How Libraries (and Other Social Infrastructure Spaces) Will Save Us: The Critical Role of Social Infrastructure in Democratic Resilience
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus
board3_verdict: social-infrastructure framing (Klinenberg lineage)

title: Public libraries to promote public health and wellbeing: a cross-sectional study of community-dwelling adults (England)
key_finding: cross-sectional: staff + users report libraries act as community hubs for wellbeing (England)
board3_verdict: the wellbeing lane (no crime endpoint)

authors: Alan Jay Lincoln, Carol Zall Lincoln
title: Library Crime in Canada
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus
board3_verdict: the library-as-crime-HOST lane (crime IN libraries, not libraries→crime)

authors: Sema A. Taheri, Brandon C. Welsh
title: After-School Programs for Delinquency Prevention
key_finding: systematic review + meta-analysis: 17 eligible ASP studies, effects on delinquency small but overall BENEFICIAL (mixed results from well-known evaluations; effect varies by program features)
board3_verdict: THE REC-CENTER META: after-school programming reduces delinquency modestly and unevenly — favorable but magnitude-fragile

title: Sports Participation and Juvenile Delinquency: A Meta-Analytic Review
key_finding: multilevel meta: 51 studies, 48 samples, 431 ES, N=132,366 — total association between sport and delinquency ≈ small/ns, sign depends on moderators
board3_verdict: THE SPORTS META: 132k adolescents — the biggest N in the whole band returns ~zero aggregate; sports is neither protective nor risk by default

title: Rethinking Sports-Based Community Crime Prevention
venue: Journal of Sport and Social Issues
key_finding: early-adopter midnight-basketball cities showed sharper property-crime DECREASES than other cities during the broad-support window (confounded; preliminary test)
board3_verdict: THE MIDNIGHT-BASKETBALL CLAUSE: the mocked program gets a surprising quasi-result — property crime falls in early-adopter cities (author-cautioned, indirect mechanisms)

title: Dosage Matters
key_finding: any dose of intensive juvenile-incarceration treatment → lower recidivism odds than none; stronger dose → significantly lower 3-y recidivism (propensity-score matching)
board3_verdict: dosage law: program intensity (not mere access) carries recidivism — the strata logic again

title: Effectiveness of a Playground Intervention for Antisocial, Prosocial, and Physical Activity Behaviors
key_finding: cluster-RCT, 4 elementary playgrounds: Peaceful Playgrounds redesign → less antisocial, more prosocial + more PA during recess
board3_verdict: the environment-redesign micro-RCT: playground build = the municipal rec-capital intervention with an actual RCT

title: Evaluation of the Peaceful Connections Violence Prevention Program: Local Evaluation Report
key_finding: BGC Santa Monica + 8 partner Clubs, 7 cities in LA County: Club-based group + individualized services for youth violence (local eval report; corpus abstract carries design not coefficients)
board3_verdict: the club-lane eval: infrastructure-anchored violence prevention, reporting to follow

authors: Krekel Christian, Kavetsos Georgios, Ziebarth Nicolas R
title: Passing on the flame: Do mega sports events promote health behaviours?
key_finding: mega-sport events (2012 London Olympics) → little/no lasting population health-behaviour improvement
board3_verdict: the negative clause: spectacle spending is NOT recreation capital

authors: Robert J. Sampson, Stephen W. Raudenbush, Felton Earls
title: Neighborhoods and Violent Crime: A Multilevel Study of Collective Efficacy
key_finding: collective efficacy → reduced violence across 343 Chicago neighborhoods, 8,782 residents; disadvantage/instability effects largely MEDIATED by collective efficacy (1995 PHDCN)
board3_verdict: THE AGGREGATION-MECHANISM CLAUSE: the causal freight of any municipal facility runs through neighborhood collective efficacy — the mediating variable for pools/parks/libraries alike

authors: Branas CC, South E, Andrulis C, et al.
title: Greening vacant lots to reduce violent crime: a randomised controlled trial
key_finding: cluster-RCT Philadelphia 541 lots/110 clusters: full greening → gun-violence reductions concentrated in most-disadvantaged neighborhoods; residents report higher perceived safety
board3_verdict: THE LOT-GREENING RCT: the best municipal-capital crime RCT in the corpus — heterogeneous by disadvantage

authors: Branas CC, South E, Kondo MC, et al.
title: Effect of Remediating Blighted Vacant Land on Shootings: A Citywide Cluster Randomized Trial
key_finding: citywide cluster-RCT (541 lots): greening → fewer firearm shootings with injury/death in below-poverty-median neighborhoods; NULL in the poorest neighborhoods
board3_verdict: THE HETEROGENEITY CLAUSE: remediation helps mid-disadvantaged blocks, NOT the poorest — the capital-spend targeting law

title: Sustainability of violence prevention after a randomized vacant lot greening intervention in Philadelphia
key_finding: 10-y follow-up of the 2013 cluster RCT: greening-score persistence 2012-2023; tests durable effect on total/violent/firearm crime per sq mile
board3_verdict: THE PERSISTENCE CLAUSE: the capital question is longevity — greening must be maintained to keep paying

authors: Kondo MC, et al. (JAMA IM team)
title: Effect of Abandoned Housing Interventions on Gun Violence, Perceptions of Safety, and Substance Use
key_finding: cluster-RCT Jan 2017-Aug 2020: abandoned-house remediation (doors/windows) → gun-violence + safety-perception improvements
board3_verdict: the structure lane (fixing buildings, not lots): same family of capital intervention, same direction

title: Impact on Family Violence of a Cluster Randomized Trial Remediating Vacant and Abandoned Property (New Orleans)
key_finding: cluster-RCT, 23 New Orleans neighborhoods 2017-2022: lot cleaning/greening + building fixes → family-violence reduction, neighborhood-characteristic modifiers
board3_verdict: remediation extends INTO the household (family violence) — municipal capital reaches private doors

authors: M. Dylan Spencer, David Mitre Becerril
title: Do Urban Greenways Reduce Crime? A Quasi-Experimental Study of the Atlanta Beltline
key_finding: Beltline corridor quasi-experiment (corpus abstract not returned; SSRN working paper)
board3_verdict: the greenway lane: the BeltLine as the recreation-capital natural experiment — carries the founder's corridor question, unreviewed

authors: South EC, Seeburger E, Dolan A, Ridgeway G, Aronowitz S, Branas CC, Perrone J, MacDonald J, Wiebe D, Mandell DS, Oyekanm
title: Neighborhood Environmental Interventions and Opioid Overdose Rates
key_finding: quasi-experimental nonrandomized (controlled interrupted time series): neighborhood environmental interventions vs opioid-overdose rates
board3_verdict: the adjacent-harm lane: the same capital lever is being tested on overdose, not just crime

title: Urban Redevelopment and Gentrification: Evidence from the Atlanta BeltLine
key_finding: not_stated_in_corpus (working paper)
board3_verdict: the displacement boundary of the capital lane: recreation capital prices out the youth it was funded for

title: Beyond Property Values: Vacant Lot Greening and Property Tax Delinquency
key_finding: 0.9pp lower tax-arrears prevalence in treated neighborhoods (3-y average); attenuates to 0.4pp matching on financial histories
board3_verdict: the fiscal side-benefit: greening pays in tax compliance, not just crime
